sections.h2: Council Bluffs and the Loess Hills
sections.html:
Council Bluffs is the seat of Pottawattamie County. It sits on the east bank of the Missouri River directly across from Omaha, Nebraska, and a small part of the city reaches into Mills County. The 2020 count was 62,799 residents, and the mid-2025 estimate is 62,680.

The city lies in the Loess Hills, so the ground rolls and drops in a way most of Iowa does not. Slope, drainage and retaining walls are normal topics when a buyer looks at a house here. The city covers about 46 square miles at 978 feet, with Lake Manawa State Park at its southern edge and viewpoints at Fairmont Park and Kirn Park.

Because the Interstate 480 bridge ties the city to downtown Omaha, a Council Bluffs house is often compared with Omaha-area options. Think about commuters on both sides of the river when you decide how to describe the house.

Named areas include Downtown, Old Town, West End, Casino Row, Twin City, Manawa, South End, Oakland-Fairview, Madison Avenue and Huntington Avenue. Mention the one your house sits in, since buyers search by area.

The river has moved the boundaries here before. Carter Lake seceded in 1926 after a change in the river's course cut it off, and an 1881 flood severed a Missouri River channel and formed Lake Manawa. If your lot is close to the water, expect a buyer to ask about floodplain status and flood history.

Two school districts divide the city. The Council Bluffs Community School District serves most of it, with 10 elementary schools, two middle schools and two high schools, Abraham Lincoln and Thomas Jefferson. The Lewis Central Community School District serves the southern part. Confirm the district for your address before you describe the house to a buyer.

Iowa bills property tax in two installments, and each has a fixed delinquent date. Iowa Code 445.37 adds timing rules that apply to Council Bluffs owners.

SituationRule
Normal delinquent datesOctober 1 for the first installment, April 1 for the second
September 30 or March 31 on a weekendDelinquency moves to the second business day of the next month
Mailed paymentThe treasurer must receive it by the last business day of the month before the delinquent date, or it must be postmarked before that date
Online paymentFollows its own midnight cutoff through a county treasurer's authorized site

If you sell mid-year, the title company usually prorates the bill. Confirm what has been paid with the Pottawattamie County Treasurer first.

sections.h2: What Iowa asks of a seller
sections.html:
Iowa wants sellers to report the condition of the land as well as the building. Under Iowa Code 558.69, a groundwater hazard statement goes to the recorder along with the declaration of value.

When none of the listed conditions exist, no separate statement is needed. The first page of the deed carries a prescribed line saying so. A recorder has to refuse a deed that lacks the required statement. The transfer tax under Iowa Code 428A.1 is 80 cents per $500, and it is not owed when no consideration is paid.

sections.h2: What to line up before closing
sections.html:
Most Council Bluffs closings go smoothly when a few items are ready early.

  • A current tax statement from the Pottawattamie County Treasurer showing both installments.
  • Notes on any well, buried tank or septic system, for the groundwater hazard statement.
  • The deed and any prior survey, so the title company can finish its search.
  • Tenant leases, if anyone lives in the house, and a plan for the move-out date.

With those in hand, a cash buyer can often work to the date you pick instead of a lender's calendar. If the house sits on a slope or near the river, add any drainage or flood paperwork to the pile.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Council Bluffs house work?
sections.html:
You tell the buyer about the house, receive a written cash offer and choose a closing date. There are no showings and no waiting on a buyer's mortgage.

  1. Share the address, the condition and any tenant or title issue.
  2. Review the written offer and ask about anything unclear.
  3. If you accept, a title company or attorney prepares the deed and the recorder filings for Pottawattamie County.
  4. Sign at closing, and the deed is recorded.

Compare the offer with the cost of repairs and the months a listing could take, and say no if it does not fit. Turning an offer down costs nothing.

sections.h2: Selling a house with tenants or an inherited title
sections.html:
Some Council Bluffs sales need a little extra planning. If tenants live in the house, get a copy of each lease and decide whether the buyer takes the house with the lease in place or whether the tenant moves out before closing. Put the move-out date in writing so the closing date can be set around it.

For an inherited house, the names on the deed must match the people signing at closing. If title is not yet in the heirs' names, start that paperwork before you ask for offers, because the recorder and the title company will both want it cleared. A cash buyer does not need a lender's sign-off on any of this, which can shorten the wait once the paperwork is right.

If the house has repairs you would rather not manage, say so up front. A cash offer reflects the condition you describe, and you decide whether the number works.

faqs.q: Is Council Bluffs the county seat of Pottawattamie County?
faqs.a: Yes. Council Bluffs is the seat of Pottawattamie County, and a small part of the city extends into Mills County.

faqs.q: How many people live in Council Bluffs?
faqs.a: The 2020 count was 62,799 residents, and the mid-2025 estimate is 62,680.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Council Bluffs house in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in the Council Bluffs Community School District. The southern part is in the Lewis Central Community School District.

faqs.q: When did Council Bluffs get its name?
faqs.a: The town was called Kanesville until about 1852 or 1853 and was incorporated as Council Bluffs on January 19, 1853. The name goes back to an 1804 meeting between Lewis and Clark and the Otoe.

faqs.q: When are Iowa property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: The first installment is delinquent from October 1 and the second from April 1. A weekend deadline moves to the second business day of the following month.
